title: Migrate feed scrolling, refresh and explicit routes
description: Use CupertinoSliverRefreshControl for iOS feed refresh and RefreshIndicator for Android; do not use RefreshIndicator.adaptive because it leaves the Material interaction structure. Let each selected app root provide scrolling physics instead of hardcoding BouncingScrollPhysics or ClampingScrollPhysics in features. Integrate the feed with PrimaryScrollController so iOS status-bar tap-to-top works while pagination, stable scroll identity, and programmatic feed scroll-to-top continue to work. Route the existing full-screen media viewer with CupertinoPageRoute on iOS and MaterialPageRoute on Android.
design: Use built-in native routes and transitions rather than custom transition implementations. Preserve iOS interactive swipe-back and Android system/predictive back. Keep refresh, pagination, filters, cache provenance, and repository/Bloc responsibilities unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: On iOS, the feed uses CupertinoSliverRefreshControl, native root scrolling behavior, PrimaryScrollController status-bar tap-to-top, existing programmatic scroll-to-top, pagination, and CupertinoPageRoute for media with interactive swipe-back. On Android, the feed uses RefreshIndicator, Material root scrolling behavior, and MaterialPageRoute with system/predictive back. No feature hardcodes platform scroll physics and RefreshIndicator.adaptive is not used as a substitute for the iOS sliver interaction. Scroll position and post identity remain stable across refresh and state changes; pagination does not duplicate requests. Route, refresh, back, and scrolling tests use stable keys/semantics/user actions, with concrete component assertions confined to platform-boundary tests.
notes: Implemented native feed mechanics: iOS inserts CupertinoSliverRefreshControl into the feed slivers; Android wraps the same CustomScrollView in RefreshIndicator. AlwaysScrollableScrollPhysics only enables short-feed refresh and composes with the selected app root's platform physics; no BouncingScrollPhysics or ClampingScrollPhysics is hardcoded. Dashboard owns and provides the feed ScrollController above AppScaffold via PrimaryScrollController, allowing CupertinoPageScaffold status-bar tap-to-top while existing programmatic top, pagination, and filter reset use the same controller. Full-screen property media selects CupertinoPageRoute on iOS and MaterialPageRoute elsewhere. Focused tests verify both real refresh controls, successful pull-to-refresh on both platforms, primary-controller identity, route class, dashboard interactions, and existing scroll/pagination behavior. Verification in direnv Flutter 3.47 shell on macOS: flutter analyze clean; flutter test 78 passed; git diff --check clean. Owner manually approved iOS pull-to-refresh, status-bar tap-to-top, and property-media swipe-back; the exact device or simulator was not named. Android system/predictive-back device evidence remains for cnr.17.6.
close_reason: Native refresh, primary scrolling, and platform media routes implemented; mobile analysis clean, 78 tests passed, diff check clean, and iOS interactions owner-approved. Exact iOS target and Android system/predictive-back evidence remain explicitly scoped to cnr.17.6.

title: Establish reusable native interaction boundaries
description: Make repeated interaction boundaries use genuine platform controls: AppIconButton uses CupertinoButton behavior on iOS and IconButton or another appropriate Material button on Android. Add a narrowly scoped AppButton only for repeated labelled actions, and add AppPressable only if concrete repeated adaptive interaction code in composed branded surfaces justifies it. Migrate repeated Material-only interaction code to these boundaries without changing product state or visual assets.
design: Every abstraction has one clear purpose and a demonstrated repeated need. Do not create a universal PlatformWidget<T, U>, mirror both component libraries in one giant button API, scatter platform conditionals through feature widgets, or replace native gesture tracking with custom machinery. Dedicated widget classes are preferred to private functions returning widgets.
acceptance_criteria: AppIconButton and any justified labelled/pressable boundary select the correct real Cupertino or Material control family. Controls preserve supplied glyph size and geometry inside ordinary minimum 48x48 activation regions, with correct semantics, labels/tooltips, focus, keyboard activation, disabled state, gesture tracking, restrained native feedback, and no duplicated callbacks. Android ink is contained; iOS uses Cupertino press behavior; green remains a selection color rather than generic press feedback. Tests prefer semantic labels, stable keys, and user actions; only focused platform-boundary tests assert concrete native control types. No speculative abstraction or new platform-widget dependency is introduced.
close_reason: Closed per owner direction (good, commit, proceed). Implementation: three narrowly scoped app_ui boundaries each select the real control family from Theme.of(context).platform in themed subtrees (never Platform.isIOS). AppIconButton: stock IconButton on Android (48px tight constraints, contained ink, own tooltip/button semantics/focus/disabled) and CupertinoButton on iOS (pressedOpacity 0.6, 48px minimum), with an optional count label announced as 'Like, 3'; unused hapticFeedback parameter removed. AppButton (new): labelled actions on the platform text-button family; call sites own text styles and pass measured minimumSize/padding/alignment/borderRadius/overlayColor/tapTargetSize. AppPressable (new): press behaviour for composed branded surfaces without owning layout — iOS CupertinoButton (pressedOpacity 0.6), Android transparency Material + contained InkResponse — with one container button-semantics node per control and an optional semantic label. Migrated without product-state or visual-asset change: post_actions _PostActionButton to AppIconButton(label); post_card profile row to AppPressable, View-all-comments to AppButton; feed_header wordmark and messages circle to AppPressable; story item, create-post prompt, property image to AppPressable; feed_view 'Try again' and OfflineStatusBar 'Retry' to AppButton. Dashboard/bottom navigation, filter sheet, notices, refresh/routes, and AppAvatar.onPressed deliberately untouched (cnr.17.3-17.5 and no production caller). Encoded probed framework behaviours: shaped Materials hit-test to their rounded path (transparency Material + DecoratedBox keeps full-box corner taps), and InkResponse lacks the button semantics flag (boundary owns a container Semantics node). Focused tests assert concrete control families per platform in app_ui only; feature tests use semantic labels, keys, and user actions. All accepted M4 geometry preserved (48px engagement, 32px text targets, 72px header, full-row profile overlay, 66px story tiles, 56px prompt). title: Establish platform roots and platform-neutral theme scope
description: Refactor the application boundary so ExpertListingApp selects CupertinoApp for iOS and MaterialApp for Android from defaultTargetPlatform, with a narrow injectable platform override for tests and no nested app roots. Introduce AppThemeScope to expose active AppColors independently of Material ThemeExtension lookup. Keep one source of truth for existing light/dark semantic palettes, build Material light/dark ThemeData and CupertinoThemeData from it, and ensure system appearance changes rebuild both Cupertino styling and AppThemeScope. Apply the same platform-root policy to the configuration-error application. Keep shared providers and Riverbloc lifecycles outside and unchanged.
design: Use Theme.of(context).platform inside themed subtrees and never Platform.isIOS. Keep Open Runde for branded feed content; allow native platform surfaces to use platform typography unless the supplied design explicitly fixes typography. - Profile build: frames=125-433 across windows; p50 16.8-33.0ms, p90 33.0-83.3ms, p99 up to ~525ms, max ~929ms; >33ms = 37-45%.

- `1.raster` thread: 529 runs / 2691ms CPU, worst single run 109.5ms. Top slices are emulator GLES-bridge encodes, not Flutter draw work: `glGenRenderbuffers encode` 1156.0ms, `glEnable encode` 463.3ms, `glDepthFunc encode` 293.8ms, `eglSwapBuffers` 143-194ms.

Empty, loading, no-result, failure, recent, and suggestion states are deliberate in light/dark mode at 360px and 428px widths. Recent searches survive provider reconstruction, are bounded, removable/clearable, and never imply server sync. Activating a suggestion produces a non-stacking exact boundary notice and no fake details route.
notes: Owner decision, 2026-09-05: autocomplete searches properties and locations, not people or general social posts. Recent search history and concise quick searches support that focused discovery model. Property suggestion activation uses the truthful property-detail preview boundary.

title: Add server-backed activity notifications
description: Replace the Notification boundary notice with an activity destination backed by Hono and Postgres, beginning with another user liking a post authored by the server-resolved current user. Define durable-versus-derived notification semantics before the migration.
design: Build after desired-state likes are real. Use a thin Hono route and vetted security-definer database function. Derive from likes if notifications may disappear on unlike; add a notification-events table only if durable history or read state is approved.
acceptance_criteria: The notification API returns only activity addressed to the request's server-resolved actor, excludes self-like noise, orders deterministically, uses safe DTOs and no raw client user ID, and exposes honest loading, empty, retry, and light/dark UI states. A real database/API journey proves another user can like the current user's post and the activity appears. Read/unread or unlike-history behavior matches the approved decision.
notes: Owner decision, 2026-09-05: like notifications are durable activity history and remain after unlike. Add a notification-events table and read state rather than deriving the inbox from current likes.

title: Build profile and safe preview user switching
description: Replace the Profile boundary notice with server-backed current-user details and a debug-only developer tool for switching among deterministic preview personas. Preserve system-controlled light/dark appearance rather than adding an in-app theme selector.
design: Add a request-scoped, server-gated preview alias mapped server-side to known fixture users; retain CURRENT_USER_ID as the default. Riverpod owns the actor context and dependent lifecycle. Do not use process-global mutable server state, production impersonation, full authentication, or a theme selector.
acceptance_criteria: Profile loads the server-resolved user's display name, handle, role, and avatar with deliberate loading/failure states and system light/dark styling. Debug builds may show a current-user switch only when the backend explicitly allows preview actors; production hides it and the server rejects overrides. The client never submits a raw user UUID. Switching actor resets/reloads feed, listing, search-sensitive, profile, and notification state so no prior actor data leaks.
notes: Owner decision, 2026-09-05: current-user switching is local-debug-only. It is hidden in release builds and requires an explicit local backend opt-in; hosted preview and production do not accept it. Profile follows system light/dark appearance and adds no theme selector.

title: Expand dashboard into real preview destinations
description: Prince directly expanded the product beyond the assessment's former out-of-scope notices: Search becomes an autocomplete experience with recents and truthful property-detail boundaries; List becomes a paginated property catalog with property-specific cards; Notification becomes a real server-backed activity home beginning with likes on the current user's posts; Profile shows current-user details and a safely gated developer current-user switch. All destinations must preserve the existing Expert Listing identity, system light/dark behavior, native platform mechanics, accessibility, stable geometry, and honest loading/error/empty states. This direct instruction supersedes the old destination notices and roadmap gate; the canonical specification must be revised before implementation claims completion.
design: Reuse app_ui tokens and controls, FeedRepository/post DTOs where their contracts fit, and Riverpod/Riverbloc lifecycle ownership. Do not add a router, second state system, ORM, service locator, local database, decorative effects, fake data success, or a production identity override. Keep the social Feed presentation separate from a property-first ListingCard. Resolve all new backend reads through thin Hono routes and vetted security-definer database functions.
acceptance_criteria: Each bottom destination has genuine selected state and preserved destination state. Search provides real autocomplete, bounded persisted recents, deliberate quick actions only where useful, and an exact property-detail preview notice. List paginates property-only server data in a property-first card layout. Notifications are returned by Hono for the server-resolved current user and include likes on that user's posts without trusting a raw client user ID. Profile renders server-backed current-user details in system light/dark themes; current-user switching is debug-only, explicitly server-gated, request-scoped, and clears actor-sensitive state. Focused state/widget/API/database tests cover race, persistence, identity, and interaction promises; named-width visual checks remain explicit evidence.

title: Cue create-post after feed readiness
description: Replace the rejected loading-time surface fade with a restrained one-shot affordance that begins only after the first visible feed data arrives.
design: FeedView passes readiness from state.posts.isNotEmpty. CreatePostPrompt owns a one-shot 1200ms outline opacity sequence composed from four AppMotion.slow intervals: 300ms ease in, a 600ms quiet peak, and 300ms ease out. Paint the border in the foreground over the existing pill; do not animate background, scale, translation, blur, gradient, or content.
acceptance_criteria: CreatePostPrompt keeps its stable subtleSurface and exact 56px geometry. Once the feed first transitions from no posts to visible posts, a thin semantic-brand outline appears and fades exactly once without moving content, replaying on refresh/filter changes, or running during initial loading. Reduced-motion users receive no animation. Activation and semantics remain unchanged, with focused timing and geometry coverage.
close_reason: Closed per owner direction (good enough, commit). Replaced the rejected loading-time surface fade with a one-shot foreground outline tied to real feed readiness: FeedView passes state.posts.isNotEmpty; CreatePostPrompt latches the first ready state, then animates a 1px semantic brand outline for 1200ms (300ms ease in, 600ms hold, 300ms ease out) while the subtleSurface, content, 56px geometry, activation, and semantics remain unchanged. Later refresh/filter state cannot replay it. MediaQuery disableAnimations skips it entirely. Evidence on macOS in direnv Flutter 3.47 shell: targeted flutter analyze clean; focused tests 2 passed for readiness timing, visible hold, no replay, stable geometry, and reduced motion; full mobile flutter analyze clean; full flutter test 75 passed; dart format clean; git diff --check clean. title: Add one-shot create-post invitation
description: The Figma-derived create-post prompt is visually quiet and can read as static content. Add a restrained, non-persistent cue that draws attention to the existing interaction without changing its geometry or adding permanent chrome.
design: Use a one-shot semantic color transition from brandTint to subtleSurface through the existing AppPressable color input and AppMotion curve. Keep the avatar, copy, padding, and pill radius unchanged. Use Duration.zero when MediaQuery disables animations.
acceptance_criteria: CreatePostPrompt briefly emphasizes its existing pill surface once when introduced, then settles to the current subtleSurface appearance without layout movement, looping, shimmer, gradients, or fake press feedback. The cue works in light and dark themes, is absent when reduced motion is requested, and does not change activation, semantics, or the 56px geometry. Focused widget coverage verifies the transient and settled states.
close_reason: Implemented a one-shot create-post invitation cue. The existing 56px AppPressable pill starts at semantic brandTint and settles to subtleSurface over AppMotion.slow with AppMotion.curve; avatar, copy, padding, radius, semantics, and activation remain unchanged. MediaQuery disableAnimations switches the transition to Duration.zero. No loop, shimmer, gradient, scaling, translation, or persistent affordance was added. Added focused widget evidence that the color passes through a transient state, reaches the original surface, and preserves the exact rectangle. Evidence on macOS in direnv Flutter 3.47 shell: targeted test passed; full apps/expert_listing_mobile flutter analyze passed; full flutter test passed 73 tests; dart format clean for touched files; git diff --check passed. title: Overlay carousel indicator on property media
description: Move the multiple-image page indicator from below the property image into the image so feed cards recover vertical space. Keep it understated and legible over both light and dark photography.
design: Use an ordinary Stack inside the existing clipped media bounds. Place a small translucent dark capsule at bottom center, with a white active mark and softened white inactive dots. Animate only dot width and opacity with the existing restrained state-transition motion and disable that animation for reduced-motion users. Do not add blur, gradients, packages, or global tokens for this one-off carousel treatment.
acceptance_criteria: The property carousel retains its stable Figma-derived image ratio, no longer reserves indicator space below the image, and shows a compact page indicator inside the image with reliable contrast over bright and dark content. Existing paging and page restoration continue to work, with focused widget coverage for placement and styling.
close_reason: Implemented and visually approved by owner on 2026-09-05. Property carousel indicator now overlays the clipped image in a translucent dark capsule, recovering the previous external xsmall gap plus indicator row while preserving 388x260 reference geometry. Active/inactive white marks remain legible over bright and dark photography; width and opacity transition over AppMotion.medium/AppMotion.curve, with Duration.zero when MediaQuery disables animations. Evidence on macOS in direnv Flutter 3.47 shell: dart format check passed for the 3 touched files; targeted flutter analyze passed for property_media.dart, post_card_test.dart, and feed_view_test.dart; targeted flutter test passed 25 tests; git diff --check passed. title: Engagement and heading controls miss 48px touch areas despite 48px semantics nodes
description: Probe-verified on Flutter 3.47: OverflowBox-sized controls (post_card heading author button, trailing overflow icon, engagement _Action rows) render a 48x48 semantics node but touch hit-testing is gated by each ancestor's size.contains, so taps only land within the parent's reserved band: 40px tall for the heading row and only 16px tall (48 wide) for the engagement actions. AppAvatar avoids this by reserving the 48px box in layout and pinning the 40px visual, which works beside a taller column but would shift sequential card content if applied to the heading or actions rows. Fixing the touch geometry requires a design decision about reserved space versus the measured Figma bands.
close_reason: Verified on Flutter 3.47 (direnv exec . flutter test test/feed/post_card_test.dart): 10/10 pass including new 'icon-only edge actions align at 428 and 360 widths'. Icon-only like/edge action targets now extend into adjacent outer space so the 48px touch band stays reachable while visible content stays on the Figma content edge; counted actions keep the counted band. Committed as 8666751. Not verified on device; no remaining surfaces in this bug.
